reconcile.connective: Defenders read the "utterly destroyed all" of 15:7-8 as a campaign total — all Saul reached — not a literal extinction, so later Amalekites are the ones who escaped.

discrepancy.connective: Thomas Paine presses the same chapters as evidence the narrative is incoherent and cruel: Saul is commanded to blot out every Amalekite, yet it is an Amalekite who later finishes Saul and carries his crown to David.

skeptic.name: Thomas Paine
skeptic.attribution: Thomas Paine (d. 1809), The Age of Reason, Part II (1795)

excerpts.excerpt_text: and utterly destroyed all the people with the edge of the sword; that is, all that came in his way, or fell into his hands; all between Havilah and Shur; all excepting those that made their escape, for we after read of Amalekites, and that in large bodies, Sa1 27:8.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly glosses the 'utterly destroyed all' clause of 15:7-8 as 'all that came in his way... all excepting those that made their escape,' and explicitly anticipates the later surviving Amalekites of 27:8 — the core harmonization of the row.

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63), on 1 Samuel 15:8 and 27:9
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: Gill treats this exact tension twice, glossing Saul's 'utterly destroyed all' as 'all that came in his way... all excepting those that made their escape,' and noting at 27:9 that David's slaughter likewise covers only 'such that came within his reach; for it is certain there were people of these several names after this.'
